page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at top centre. A handwritten or stray "317" at the top right is outside the printed page and is not transcribed. Text runs continuously from the previous page to a catchword at the lower right. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: effusum; converte me, ut convertar, quia tu es Iehova Deus meus.

Nam postquam conversus fuero, poenitebit me, & postquam ostensum fuerit mihi, applaudam femori (dolens gravissimè) erubesco, etiamque suffundar rubore, quod sciam opprobrium puerilitia mea. & v.33.34.

Nam hoc illud est foedus, quod pangam cum domo Israelis: Post dies illos, dictum Iehova, indam legem meam mentibus[?] eorum, & cordibus[?] eorum inscribam eam: & ero eis Deus, & ipsi erunt mihi populus.

Non autem (solum) docebunt amplius quisque amicum suum, & quisque[?] fratrem suum, dicendo: cognoscite Iehovam: Nam quotquot erunt, cognoscent me a minimo eorum, usque ad maximum eorum, dictum Iehova (nempe) me condonare iniquitatem ipsorum, & peccati ipsorum non recordari amplius. Et certe resipiscentia, ut effectus, fidem causam suam sequi solet.

Nam dolor ille, qui est secundum Deum, & efficit resipiscentiam, mentisque & consilii immutationem, item voluntatis & cordis conversionem, a malo & peccato commisso, ad bonum in posterum faciendum, fidei potius fœtus est.

page.notes: The running head is followed by a small mark at the right ("sœ" or similar) that is unclear and was left out. The handwritten "317" at the top right is not printed text and was left out. Printed "dictum" and "dies" have long-s forms that were read as plain s. Words marked [?] (mentibus, cordibus, quisque in "quisque fratrem") are abbreviated in print and could not be read with certainty. The first word of the page ("effusum") is a fragment carried over from the previous page and was read with some doubt. Faint show-through from the reverse side is visible in the right margin and was not transcribed.
